_metadata.title: ComplianceLint Interim Standard for EU AI Act Article 26: Obligations of Deployers
_metadata.disclaimer: This is an interim checklist developed by ComplianceLint. It is not a harmonised standard and does not itself give a presumption of conformity. No harmonised standard is requested specifically for Article 26 in the Commission's standardisation request (Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 3871). Article 96(1)(a) requires Commission guidelines on the practical application of Article 26.
basis: EU AI Act Recitals 91-93 (legislative intent on deployer obligations)
GDPR Articles 35, 36 -- Data protection impact assessment
_metadata.awaiting_standard: No harmonised standard is requested specifically for Article 26 in the Commission's standardisation request (Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 3871). Article 96(1)(a) requires Commission guidelines on the practical application of Article 26.

requirements.title: Deployment Documentation
requirements.requirement: The deployer MUST take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure that it uses the high-risk AI system in accordance with the instructions for use accompanying the system (Article 26(1)). The deployer SHOULD document those measures; Article 26(1) does not require such documentation.
requirements.rationale: Art. 26(1) requires deployers to 'take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions for use accompanying the systems'. Documentation of those measures provides evidence of compliance.
required_content: Reference to provider's instructions for use
Escalation procedures for anomalies or risks

requirements.title: Human Oversight Assignment
requirements.requirement: The deployer MUST assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support (Article 26(2)). The deployer SHOULD document the assignment and the competence of the persons assigned. Article 26(3) preserves the deployer's freedom to organise its own resources and activities for the purpose of implementing the human oversight measures indicated by the provider.
requirements.rationale: Art. 26(2) requires oversight by natural persons with 'the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support'. Documenting the assignment is recommended practice; Art. 26(2) does not require it.
required_content: Competency requirements and evidence of training
Authority scope (what they can override or stop)

requirements.title: Operational Monitoring
requirements.requirement: The deployer MUST monitor the operation of the high-risk AI system on the basis of the instructions for use and, where relevant, inform providers in accordance with Article 72. Where the deployer has reason to consider that use in accordance with the instructions may result in the system presenting a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1), it MUST, without undue delay, inform the provider or distributor and the relevant market surveillance authority, and suspend the use of the system. Where the deployer has identified a serious incident, it MUST also immediately inform first the provider, and then the importer or distributor and the relevant market surveillance authorities; if it is not able to reach the provider, Article 73 applies mutatis mutandis (Article 26(5), first subparagraph). This obligation does not cover sensitive operational data of deployers of AI systems which are law enforcement authorities. For deployers that are financial institutions subject to requirements regarding their internal governance, arrangements or processes under Union financial services law, the monitoring obligation is deemed to be fulfilled by complying with the rules on internal governance arrangements, processes and mechanisms pursuant to the relevant financial service law (Article 26(5), second subparagraph).
requirements.rationale: Art. 26(5) requires monitoring 'on the basis of the instructions for use' and sets duties to inform the provider, the importer or distributor and the market surveillance authorities, and to suspend use, in the cases it lists. The duty does not cover sensitive operational data of deployers of AI systems which are law enforcement authorities.
acceptable_implementations: Monitoring dashboards with AI system health metrics
Regular performance reviews against provider specifications
Provider communication channel for risk reporting

requirements.title: Log Retention
requirements.requirement: The deployer MUST keep the logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system, to the extent such logs are under its control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in applicable Union or national law, in particular in Union law on the protection of personal data (Article 26(6)). Deployers that are financial institutions subject to Union financial services law on internal governance maintain the logs as part of the documentation kept under that law.
requirements.rationale: Art. 26(6) sets a retention period for deployers of 'at least six months', limited to logs under the deployer's control and subject to applicable Union or national law.
acceptable_implementations: Log storage with a configured retention of 184 days (at least six months)
Cloud logging service with retention policy
Log archive system with documented retention period

requirements.title: Affected Person Notification
requirements.requirement: Deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III that make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons MUST inform those natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system, without prejudice to Article 50 (Article 26(11)). For high-risk AI systems used for law enforcement purposes, Article 13 of Directive (EU) 2016/680 applies.
requirements.rationale: Art. 26(11) requires transparency to affected persons.
acceptable_implementations: Clear AI disclosure in user-facing interfaces
Terms of service with AI usage disclosure
Physical signage for in-person AI systems

scoring.compliant: R01 + R02 + R03 + R04 + R05 all met
scoring.partial: R01 or R02 met, but not all of R01 to R05
